title: One [roles] table cannot carry both herdr and pi routing; this repo pi routing was retargeted
description:
BLOCKER, finding 2 of the final review. capabilityLabel() emits model[:effort] and DROPS kind, but those strings become pi --provider/--model/--thinking (supervisor.ts:118-120). The schema says Model is "in the kinds own namespace", so a [roles] table written for kind = claude hands claude-namespace ids to a pi subprocess.

After sqt migrated this repo, loadRunnerConfig on the current tree gives:
  planner_model            openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol:xhigh -> sonnet:high
  scout_model              openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol:low   -> sonnet:high
  review_model             openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol:xhigh -> sonnet:high
  closeout_model           (unset -> planner)             -> sonnet:high
  implement_economy_model  ...:low                        -> haiku:low
  implement_balanced_model ...:medium                     -> gpt-5.6-luna:max  (codex id, kind dropped)
  implement_strong_model   ...:high                       -> opus:high
  maxParallel              4                              -> 3
No provider is passed at all any more. /ticks-plan and /ticks-run in THIS repo now dispatch pi with claude and codex ids.

In fairness the migrator warned on 6 of these and documented the judgement call. What it did not report is the STRUCTURAL limit tick 728 asked for in writing: one [roles] table cannot simultaneously express a herdr/claude routing and a pi routing. The migrator warns which value won, never which READER the winning value is for. The comment now in .tick/runners.toml — that these roles resolving against [roles.implement] is "exactly what they did before the migration" — is true for tk herd spawn and FALSE for the pi extension, the only consumer those Pi Orchestrator keys ever had.

Needs an operator decision, then a fix. Recommended: fail closed — the pi extension refuses to read a role whose kind is not pi, naming the kind mismatch — because silently dispatching pi with claude ids is the worst of the three outcomes. If this repos pi routing is to be restored, it needs a shape that can hold per-substrate routing rather than one shared table.
notes:
2026-08-19 23:54 - Operator decision (human, 2026-08-19): FAIL CLOSED. The pi extension must refuse to derive a pi --provider/--model from a role whose kind is not pi, naming the kind mismatch, rather than silently handing claude/codex namespace ids to a pi subprocess. Do NOT build per-substrate routing tables in this tick — that is a larger shape change and was not chosen.

For this repo specifically: after the refusal exists, either restore working pi routing under whatever the chosen shape supports, or record explicitly in .tick/runners.toml that this repo does not use the pi extension. Do not leave it in the current state, where /ticks-plan and /ticks-run would dispatch pi with claude and codex model ids and no provider.

Note fdo has already landed and changed neighbouring code: review/closeout/scout no longer fall back to roles.implement on the TOML path. Read the current state of readRouting before editing.

acceptance_criteria: The pi extension never derives a pi --provider/--model from a role whose kind is not pi; whichever policy is chosen (refuse, or per-substrate routing) is documented in runners-config.md and covered by a test; this repo either has working pi routing again or an explicit recorded decision that it does not use pi.
closed_reason: Completed: the pi extension now refuses a role whose kind is not pi rather than handing claude/codex model ids to a pi subprocess, with the refusal surfaced as a config error that blocks the run; this repo's position recorded explicitly (herdr substrate with claude/codex workers, pi not used) so the state is deliberate rather than accidental.
